declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurveLt
declarations.statement: def: galileoCurveLt n U p q := ∃ γ : ℝ → ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ), ContinuousOn γ (Icc 0 1) ∧ γ 0 = p ∧ γ 1 = q ∧ MapsTo γ (Icc 0 1) U ∧ StrictMonoOn (fun s => (γ s).1) (Icc 0 1)
declarations.standing: The target's chronological relation, verbatim: a continuous curve of U with strictly increasing time runs from p to q.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve
declarations.statement: def galileoCurve (n : ℕ) : Causality (ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ)); le U p q := galileoCurveLt n U p q ∨ (p = q ∧ p ∈ U), lt := galileoCurveLt n
declarations.standing: The model. Every field is proved: transitivity by concatenation of graphs; I^±_U(x) open (isOpen_galileoGraphLt_right/_left: a point of the curve just before y, then straight segments in a small ball). No sorry in any field.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurveLt_iff_graphLt
declarations.statement: galileoCurveLt n U p q ↔ galileoGraphLt n U p q (p.1 < q.1 ∧ ∃ f continuous, f p.1 = p.2, f q.1 = q.2, ∀ t ∈ Icc p.1 q.1, (t, f t) ∈ U)
declarations.standing: The curve form reparametrised by time. Curve to graph: the curve is a CurveOn of the graph relations (straight segments in small balls), then CurveOn.rel_of_lt; no inverse of the time function needed. Graph to curve: s ↦ (p.1 + s(q.1 − p.1), f(…)).

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_chronalCurveOn_iff
declarations.statement: (galileoCurve n).ChronalCurveOn W c a b ↔ ContinuousOn c (Icc a b) ∧ MapsTo c (Icc a b) W ∧ StrictMonoOn (fun s => (c s).1) (Icc a b)
declarations.standing: Every W. The chronal curves are the continuous time-increasing maps.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_causallyArcConnected
declarations.standing: Every n.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_pushUp
declarations.standing: Every n. ≤ is = or ≪.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_chronalNeighbours
declarations.standing: Every n. The points of V just before and just after v on its vertical.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_isCausal
declarations.standing: Every n.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_hasTimeFunction
declarations.standing: Every n; T = Prod.fst.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_isTimeFunction_fst
declarations.standing: Every n. defi:fonction_temps (DEC-10): a strong morphism to timelikeLine (continuous, open, and a curve of fst⁻¹ U passes every time between its ends).

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_futureOneConnectedOn
declarations.standing: Every n, every convex open W: the convex combination (1 − t)γ₀ + tγ₁ is a chronal homotopy (galileoCurve_chronalHomotopyOn_convexCombination, :474). galileoCurve_futureOneConnected (:515) is W = ⊤.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_diamond_top
declarations.statement: p.1 < q.1 → (galileoCurve n).diamond ⊤ p q = {r | p.1 < r.1 ∧ r.1 < q.1} ∪ {p, q}
declarations.standing: Every n; as galileoOn_diamond_top for the printed causality.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_slab_subset_of_convex
declarations.statement: Convex ℝ (W : Set _) → (galileoCurve n).CausallyConvexIn V W → p ∈ V → q ∈ V → {r | r ∈ W ∧ p.1 < r.1 ∧ r.1 < q.1} ⊆ V
declarations.standing: Every n. The ladder note's slab argument in a convex open W, verbatim.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_not_causallyCompact
declarations.standing: J((0,0),(2,0)) holds (1, (B+1, …)) for every B: its first spatial coordinate is unbounded.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_not_stronglyCausalOn
declarations.standing: Stronger than the target: no non-empty open set is strongly causal as a spacetime. The slab argument in a ball B ⊆ W about p.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_not_locallyStronglyCausal
declarations.standing: From galileoCurve_not_stronglyCausalOn at the origin.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_lt_imp_galileo
declarations.statement: (galileoCurve n).lt U p q → (galileo n).lt U p q
declarations.standing: Every open U: the curve form is finer than the printed causality (a curve lies in one component). galileoCurve_le_imp_galileo (:615) for ≤.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_lt_iff_galileo_of_convex
declarations.statement: Convex ℝ (U : Set _) → ((galileoCurve n).lt U p q ↔ (galileo n).lt U p q)
declarations.standing: The agreement on convex opens the dispatch allows (the straight segment). galileoCurve_le_iff_galileo_of_convex (:627) for ≤.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_lt_iff_transGen_convex
declarations.statement: ∀ S open cover, (galileoCurve n).lt U p q ↔ TransGen (fun a b => ∃ B, ∃ O ∈ S, B ≤ U ⊓ O ∧ Convex ℝ B ∧ (galileo n).lt B a b) p q
declarations.standing: The curve form is generated, by chains, by the printed relations of the convex open subsets of the members of any open cover. Information for OQ-108 (a); decides nothing.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_ne_galileo
declarations.standing: One is absolutely minimal, the other is not (Causal.GluingModels.galileo_not_minimal). exists_galileo_lt_not_galileoCurve_lt (:689): some U, p, q with (galileo n).lt U p q and ¬ (galileoCurve n).lt U p q.

declarations.name: Causal.galileoCurve_separates
declarations.statement: 1 ≤ n → (galileoCurve n).CausallyArcConnected ∧ AbsolutelyMinimal ∧ (∀ W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W) ∧ PushUp ∧ LocallyPushUp ∧ CausallyOpen ∧ CausallyOpenFuture ∧ LocallyCausallyOpen ∧ LocallyCausallyOpenFuture ∧ Tarentin ∧ ChronalNeighbours ∧ HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere ∧ CausallyPlain ∧ IsCausal ∧ HasTimeFunction ∧ IsTimeFunction Prod.fst ∧ FutureOneConnected ∧ CurvesExtend ∧ ¬ LocallyStronglyCausal ∧ ¬ StronglyCausal ∧ ¬ StronglyCausalOpen ∧ ¬ CausallyCompact ∧ ¬ GloballyHyperbolic (all of galileoCurve n)
declarations.standing: The conjoined theorem. 23 conjuncts; it decides all 21 causality-sort nodes (16 hold, 5 fail). The only hypothesis is 1 ≤ n, used only by the negative conjuncts. Proved directly: arc-connectedness, push-up, chronal neighbours, the two time-function conjuncts, future one-connectedness, ¬ LocallyStronglyCausal, ¬ CausallyCompact, and ∀ W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W (CausallyArcConnectedOn.absolutelyMinimalOn). Everything else comes by causal_ladder: absolutely_minimal, causally_open (push_up ∧ chronal_neighbours), causally_open_future, both local forms, tarentin, has_chronal_neighbour, causally_plain, locally_push_up, is_causal, curves_extend. The negations ¬ StronglyCausal, ¬ StronglyCausalOpen and ¬ GloballyHyperbolic are causal_ladder under a negation.

questions: OQ-108 (OPEN). I decided no reading and marked no label. Here is what the file adds for the author. Read 'the causality its small open sets generate' as chains of printed relations inside small convex open sets. Then reading (a) is exactly this curve form: galileoCurve_lt_iff_transGen_convex proves it, for the convex open subsets of the members of any open cover. Read 'generate' as the library's Precausality.generated over a cover (relations in V ⊓ O). Then the result is argued to be a different causality: on every open V inside a member of the cover, generation returns the printed relation of V itself. A cup-shaped V, as in galileoOn_not_minimal, scaled into one member, relates across the bend, which the curve form does not. This is argued, not in Lean. So reading (a) needs the word 'generate' fixed before the curve form can be its formalization.

The reading of 'continuous curve' in the target. I took γ : ℝ → ℝ × ℝⁿ continuous on [0, 1], with γ 0 = x, γ 1 = y, γ([0, 1]) ⊆ U and strictly increasing time. The choice does not matter. The same relation comes from curves over any segment (galileoCurveLt_of_continuousOn), from graphs of continuous functions of time (galileoCurveLt_iff_graphLt), and from polygonal paths (galileoCurve_lt_iff_transGen_convex: chains of straight segments).

The dimension. The target says n ≥ 1 (n = 1 suffices). I state every result for all n ≥ 1, the positive ones for every n. Probe.lean instantiates n = 1. For n = 0 the negative conjuncts are not claimed.
The `from` of the new [[fails]] entry is the keeper's call. The simulation shows the full 16-id from settles all 16 pairs. The dispatch's 8 ids alone settle 9 (B). One entry per pair would also work.
kb_proposals: Galileo's spacetime in its curve form, Causal.galileoCurve n (CausalScaffold.GalileoCurveForm). It is an ETT-layer causality on ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ): ≪_U is along continuous curves of U with strictly increasing time. It is causally arc-connected, absolutely minimal on every open set, push-up, causally open, tarentin, plain, with chronal neighbours, a time function and future one-connected. It is not locally strongly causal; for n ≥ 1 no non-empty open set is strongly causal. galileoCurve_separates decides all 21 causality nodes. It is the printed galileo n on convex opens and differs from it elsewhere (T-abs-galileo-curve-form).

To show that a relation defined by curves holds between a curve's ends without inverting a time function: show that the relation family is an IsRelFamily, show that the curve is a CurveOn of it (locally, straight segments in small balls), then apply CurveOn.rel_of_lt. This is galileoCurveLt_iff_graphLt and galileoCurve_lt_iff_transGen_convex, with no Lebesgue number and no inverse function (T-abs-galileo-curve-form).
